lines.text: Cancer is a word. Waiting is a number.
A computer can never be held accountable. We agree.
So ours never decides. Each dot is a simulated patient. The piles are waiting: eighty-seven percent of the days.
The pathway is a flowchart. At each step, a model reads the notes, compares every option at once, and proposes the next step. A second opinion. An optimiser for the order.
A real Norwegian pathway, rebuilt from the paper: forty percent on time, as published. The time goes into queues.
Told nothing, the optimiser finds the authors' reorder. Eighty percent. More capacity barely moves it. Order does.
In a synthetic Finnish county, eighteen percent are treated within ninety days. With two reorders and no new equipment, thirty-three.
A doctor decides every case. Waiting is a decision nobody made. Now someone can.
